target.how: npm install theokit@0.70.0 into a throwaway project; the published tarball, never the working tree

results.note: the HITL approval path needs a booted agent server driven by two distinct identities. The published client surface is approve(approvalId, decision) with no subject, so ownership can only be observed server-side, over the wire. Not driven in this run.

the PRIMITIVE passed 4/4 against the published build: owner allowed; a different authenticated caller refused with 'subject does not own this resource'; an unauthenticated caller refused with 'not authenticated'; a resource with no recorded owner refused rather than allowed (fail-safe). The CRITERION is about the approval PATH, and a correct primitive does not prove the path calls it. ROADMAP names the remaining gap itself: the approval ledger records no owner. Path not driven.

the server-boundary gate could not be armed outside a real build. theoPlugin() yields one plugin with enforce=undefined, while ROADMAP describes the gate as a resolveId hook at enforce:'pre'. Calling resolveId directly after config() passed a server subpath through from a .client.tsx importer under ssr false, true and absent. That is a harness that did not arm the control, NOT a demonstration that the control is broken. Proving it needs a real vite build in a scaffolded app.

3/3 against the published build with NO csrf option passed anywhere. Cross-origin POST with no token: 403 FORBIDDEN, 'CSRF check failed: Missing X-Theo-Action header' — refused by the gate, by name. Same-origin POST carrying the header: 200. Cross-origin GET: 200, so the default does not over-block a non-state-changing request. The route is authored the way the published README authors one; three earlier guesses at the API produced 405 and 500 — rejections for the wrong reason, which read exactly like the right answer.
Web was partially exercised (AC4). Tauri and TUI were not exercised at all in this run.
Tauri authorization ADR. ROADMAP itself records the breaking half as outstanding: absence stops meaning open, and session.ts loses ServerResponse.
